## <a id="what-is-uncensored-ai-studio"></a>📖 What is Portable AI Studio?

**Portable AI Studio** is a completely offline, zero-setup, self-contained AI studio for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Unlike cloud-based AI systems, it runs entirely on your own hardware with no censorship, tracking, subscriptions, or login requirements.

It unifies four major local AI capabilities into one high-performance desktop interface:
1. **🎨 Image Generation (Stable Diffusion):** Generate and edit high-quality images offline using `.safetensors`, `.gguf`, or `.ckpt` model weights.
2. **💬 Text Chat (LLMs):** Converse privately with open-source language models (GGUF format) powered by official, high-performance `llama.cpp` backends.
3. **🎙️ Speech-to-Text (Whisper):** Transcribe voice recordings and speech to text in real-time with an integrated `whisper.cpp` engine.
4. **🗣️ Text-to-Speech (Kokoro TTS):** Convert text outputs into highly natural, lifelike vocal audio offline using the `Kokoro-82M` ONNX model.

---

## <a id="key-features"></a>🌟 Key Features

*   **100% Offline & Private:** Run inferences locally. No internet, telemetry, cloud logging, or API keys required.
*   **Zero-Install Portability:** Entire runtime (Node.js, models, GPU backends) is self-contained. Zero global system environment changes.
*   **Auto-Configured Acceleration:** Auto-detects hardware specs to load CUDA (Nvidia), ROCm (AMD), Vulkan (Intel/AMD/NVIDIA), Metal (macOS), or OpenVINO (Intel NPU) backends.
*   **Integrated Model Manager:** Paste Hugging Face URLs to download weights directly, or drag-and-drop local weights to import them.
*   **Live Performance Monitor:** Track CPU, RAM, GPU, and VRAM utilization in real-time directly inside the web UI.
*   **Local Output Gallery:** Saves generated images side-by-side with prompt parameters and metadata JSON files.

---

## <a id="workspace-architecture"></a>⚙️ Workspace & Engine Architecture

To avoid exhausting system RAM or VRAM, text and image engines are mutually exclusive by default. You can switch between workspaces inside the UI:

*   **Image Generation Workspace:** Uses a dedicated `stable-diffusion.cpp` backend node. Model weights are stored in `app/models/`.
*   **Text Chat Workspace:** Uses a portable `llama.cpp` server backend. Model weights (.gguf) are stored in `app/llm-models/`. A small Qwen2.5 Coder starter model can be downloaded directly from the Text Chat panel.
*   **Speech Worker (Whisper):** Runs a localized `whisper-cli` process to convert your vocal input to text.
*   **Audio Output (Kokoro TTS):** Utilizes `kokoro-js` locally on the server side to read responses in natural voices.

---

## <a id="supported-models"></a>Supported Models

The app is designed around single-file local models that can be loaded directly by the bundled backend engines.

### Image generation

| Model type | Supported | Put files in | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Stable Diffusion 1.5 checkpoints | Yes | `app/models/` | Best compatibility. Use `.safetensors` or `.ckpt` files. |
| SDXL checkpoints | Yes | `app/models/` | Supported as single-file checkpoints. Requires more RAM/VRAM than SD 1.5. |
| Single-file SD/SDXL GGUF checkpoints | Limited | `app/models/` | Only complete single-file checkpoints are supported. |
| OpenVINO image model folders | Intel NPU only | `app/openvino-models/` | Download from the Model Manager after running the OpenVINO setup. |
| CoreML image models | Apple Silicon only | `app/models/` | Requires macOS on Apple Silicon and the CoreML setup path. |
| Flux, HiDream, Hunyuan, Wan, Qwen Image, Z-Image workflows | No | N/A | These usually require separate diffusion, VAE, and text encoder files and are not one-click checkpoint loads in this app. |
| LoRA, ControlNet, VAE-only, text-encoder-only, or diffusion-only files | No | N/A | Companion files are not loaded as standalone image models. |

Known-good image models available from the Model Manager:

| Name | Filename | Type | Approx. size | Recommended use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Juggernaut XL v9 Lightning | `Juggernaut_RunDiffusionPhoto2_Lightning_4Steps.safetensors` | SDXL | 7.1 GB | High-quality photorealism on mid/high tier machines. |
| DreamShaper XL Lightning | `DreamShaperXL_Lightning.safetensors` | SDXL | 6.9 GB | General SDXL images, fantasy, renders, and illustration. |
| DreamShaper 8 | `DreamShaper_8_pruned.safetensors` | SD 1.5 | 2.1 GB | Faster, lower-memory image generation. |
| CyberRealistic V8 | `CyberRealistic_V8_FP16.safetensors` | SD 1.5 | 2.0 GB | Realistic SD 1.5 images and lower-memory systems. |
| Rev Animated | `rev-animated-v1-2-2.safetensors` | SD 1.5 | 2.0 GB | Stylized/anime SD 1.5 images. |
| LCM DreamShaper OpenVINO | `OpenVINO/LCM_Dreamshaper_v7-fp16-ov` | OpenVINO | 2.7 GB | Intel Core Ultra NPU test model. |

### Text, speech, and TTS

| Workspace | Supported model files | Put files in | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Text Chat | `.gguf` llama.cpp models | `app/llm-models/` | Use single-file GGUF chat/instruct models. Vision models may also require a matching `mmproj` file. |
| Speech-to-Text | whisper.cpp `.bin` models | `app/speech-models/` | Use Whisper GGML/whisper.cpp model files. |
| Text-to-Speech | Kokoro `.json` manifests and model assets | `app/tts-models/` / `app/tts-runtime/` | Use the built-in Kokoro setup and Model Manager entries. |

> [!NOTE]
> Linux release binaries are built for Ubuntu 24.04-era systems and require `glibc 2.38+` plus `GLIBCXX_3.4.32+`. On older Ubuntu/Debian VMs, a model such as CyberRealistic may be valid but the backend can still fail before loading it. Upgrade the VM OS or build the backend from source.

## <a id="getting-started"></a>🚀 Getting Started

Ensure you have a modern web browser installed. Follow the quick guide below for your platform:

### Windows Setup

1. **Launch:** Double-click **`windows.bat`**.
   > [!NOTE]
   > On the first run, the script will automatically download a portable Node.js runtime and configure pre-compiled GPU/CPU backend binaries.
2. **Add Models:** Drop `.safetensors`, `.gguf`, or `.ckpt` weights into `app/models/` (or download them via the **Model Manager** tab in the UI).
3. **Generate:** Open `http://localhost:1420` in your browser, select your model, and write a prompt.

### Linux Setup

1. **Make executable:** Open a terminal in the project folder and make the script executable:
   ```bash
   chmod +x linux.sh
   ```
2. **Launch:** Run **`./linux.sh`**.
   - **NVIDIA GPU Users:** You will be prompted to set up the high-performance **CUDA** backend (downloads prebuilt or automatically compiles from source as a fallback).
   - **AMD Radeon Performance:** Run with **`./linux.sh --max-perf`** to add the ROCm backend (~1.3 GB download).
   - **Intel Core Ultra NPU:** Run with **`./linux.sh --setup-openvino`** to configure Intel NPU support (requires Intel Linux NPU driver).
3. **Add Models:** Drop your weights into `app/models/` or download them via the **Model Manager** tab.
4. **Generate:** Open `http://localhost:1420` in your browser.

### macOS Setup

1. **Make executable:** Open a terminal in the project folder and make the script executable:
   ```bash
   chmod +x mac.sh
   ```
2. **Launch:** Run **`./mac.sh`**.
   > [!IMPORTANT]
   > The prebuilt macOS backend is optimized for **Apple Silicon (M1 or newer)** and uses **Metal** GPU acceleration. *(macOS Intel hardware is completely unsupported)*.
3. **Add Models:** Drop your weights into `app/models/` or download them via the **Model Manager** tab.
4. **Generate:** Open `http://localhost:1420` in your browser.

## <a id="hardware-compatibility-acceleration"></a>🖥️ Hardware Compatibility & Acceleration

### Windows

| GPU Vendor | Tech | Status | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nvidia** | CUDA | ✅ Native | Maps `sd-cuda.exe` with Nvidia SDK 12 optimizations. |
| **AMD Radeon** | Vulkan | ✅ Native | Maps `sd-vulkan.exe` with Vulkan API acceleration. |
| **Intel Arc** | Vulkan | ✅ Native | Maps `sd-vulkan.exe` for Intel hardware. |
| **Integrated / None** | CPU | ⚠️ Fallback | Runs on logical CPU threads (slow). |

### Linux

| GPU Vendor | Primary | Fallback | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **NVIDIA** | CUDA / Vulkan | Vulkan / CPU | Auto-detects NVIDIA. Prompt-driven CUDA setup downloads prebuilt or compiles from source. Falls back to Vulkan for GTX. |
| **AMD Radeon** | ROCm | Vulkan | ROCm provides best AMD performance when host ROCm drivers are available. |
| **Intel Arc / integrated** | Vulkan | CPU | Cross-vendor Vulkan support. |
| **Intel Core Ultra NPU** | OpenVINO NPU | CPU | Requires the Intel Linux NPU driver, kernel 6.6+, Python 3, and `./linux.sh --setup-openvino`. |
| **Integrated / None** | CPU | — | Runs on logical CPU threads (slow). |

### macOS

| Hardware | Primary | Fallback | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Apple Silicon (M1 or newer)** | Metal | CPU | Uses the official Darwin arm64 stable-diffusion.cpp backend. |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **System Requirements & Notes:**
> - **64-bit Windows 10 or Windows 11** is required for the portable Node.js 22 runtime used by the Windows launcher.
> - **glibc 2.38 or newer** is required for the prebuilt Linux backends (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40+, etc.). The setup script will warn you if your glibc is older.
> - **Linux runtime libraries:** The prebuilt backends require `libgomp.so.1`; Vulkan additionally requires `libvulkan.so.1` and a working GPU driver. The setup script now checks these before installing a backend and prints the exact distro package command when one is missing.
> - **Linux OpenVINO NPU:** Intel Core Ultra, x86_64 Linux, kernel 6.6+, a working `/dev/accel/accel0` device, Python 3 with `venv`, and the Intel Linux NPU driver are required.

---

## <a id="troubleshooting-faq"></a>🛠️ Troubleshooting & FAQ

<details>
  <summary><strong> Reset Environment: If a build fails or you want to clear dependencies</strong></summary>
  <p>Run <code>scripts/reset/reset.ps1</code> (Windows) or <code>scripts/reset/reset.sh</code> (Linux/macOS). This will clear temporary compilation and package caches to repair your environment. <em>(Note: This preserves your model weights and generated output images).</em></p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Linux backends fail to start with <code>GLIBC_2.38 not found</code></strong></summary>
  <p>The prebuilt binaries require glibc 2.38+ (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04). If your distribution uses an older glibc version, you can upgrade your operating system or compile the backend from source (see the <a href="#building-from-source">Building From Source</a> guide below).</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Port Conflicts: Default port address already busy</strong></summary>
  <p>The web user interface runs on port <code>1420</code> by default. The GPU backend manager attempts to bind to port <code>8080</code> first, then automatically detects and falls back to a free system port if <code>8080</code> is already occupied.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Opening the studio from another device on your network</strong></summary>
  <p>The web interface only accepts connections from the computer it runs on, because it has no login. To reach it from another device on purpose, start it with <code>UAIS_HOST=0.0.0.0</code> (for example <code>UAIS_HOST=0.0.0.0 ./linux.sh</code>, or <code>set UAIS_HOST=0.0.0.0</code> before running <code>windows.bat</code>). Anyone on that network can then use it.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Linux ROCm not loading for AMD Radeon GPUs</strong></summary>
  <p>Ensure your AMD GPU hardware and host kernel are fully compatible with ROCm 7.13. If ROCm fails to initialize correctly, the application will automatically fall back to Vulkan acceleration.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Linux uses the integrated GPU instead of the discrete GPU</strong></summary>
  <p>On dual-GPU Linux systems, Vulkan device order can put the integrated Intel GPU at <code>vulkan0</code> and the discrete AMD/NVIDIA GPU at <code>vulkan1</code>. The launcher now tries to prefer a discrete Vulkan device when <code>vulkaninfo --summary</code> is available. To force a device manually, start the app with <code>SD_VULKAN_DEVICE=vulkan1 ./linux.sh</code> or use another index such as <code>vulkan0</code>/<code>vulkan2</code>.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Windows exits with code <code>3221225781</code> (0xC0000135)</strong></summary>
  <p>This code means Windows could not locate a required backend DLL:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>For AMD/Intel Vulkan:</strong> Rerun <code>scripts/setup/setup.ps1</code>. Setup installs the required Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime and replaces stale Vulkan binaries with the compatible pinned build. Approve the Windows administrator prompt when it appears.</li>
    <li><strong>For NVIDIA CUDA:</strong> Install or update your NVIDIA graphics driver, then rerun the setup script to restore the CUDA runtime DLLs.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>If setup cannot install the runtime, install Microsoft's official <a href="https://aka.ms/vc14/vc_redist.x64.exe">Visual C++ Redistributable for x64</a> manually, restart Windows, and rerun setup. A custom Vulkan build is not the first fix for this exit code.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Windows exits with code <code>3221225501</code> (0xC000001D)</strong></summary>
  <p>This is an illegal CPU instruction from an older machine-specific Windows backend build; it is not evidence that the model or RTX GPU is unsupported. Rerun <code>scripts/setup/setup.ps1</code> to replace the CPU/CUDA binaries with runtime-dispatched builds and install the matching CUDA 12.8 runtime. The corrected CUDA package includes Blackwell targets for RTX 50-series GPUs.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Generation shows "server is not responding or crashed"</strong></summary>
  <p>This indicates that the local backend engine process terminated. Check your launch terminal (where you executed <code>windows.bat</code>, <code>./linux.sh</code>, or <code>./mac.sh</code>) for the exact console error. Common causes include glibc version mismatches, missing Vulkan drivers, or system out-of-memory (OOM) issues.</p>
</details>

---

## <a id="building-from-source"></a>🔨 Building From Source

The setup script (`scripts/setup/setup.sh`) now automates building and setting up the CUDA backend from source when selected. If you want to manually build all backends (CPU, Vulkan, and CUDA) at once, you can run the included `scripts/build/build_from_source.sh` script.

# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

<p align="left">
  <strong>English</strong> · <a href="README_ZH.md">简体中文 (Chinese)</a>
</p>

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History**

[**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en)

*The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

<p align="center">

    <img src="assets/hero_demo_en.webp" alt="Chronicles of the Realm — 15s Interactive Overview (Warring States Unification, 2,400-Year Dynastic Scrubbing, Chang'an Place Genealogy & Su Shi's Exile Route)" width="100%" />
  </a>
</p>

---

## Why It's Fun to Explore

Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry:
- *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"*
- *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"*
- *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"*

**Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time.

---

### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders

- **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to zoom straight to it.
- **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Hami & Seven Guards West of Jiayuguan (1404 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible.
- **Inline Reigning Monarch & Imperial Era Display**: The timeline dynamically displays the reigning monarch (temple/posthumous title + personal name + reign span, e.g., `Emperor Wu of Han · Liu Che`, `Emperor Taizong of Tang · Li Shimin`, `Emperor Shengzu of Qing · Xuanye`) alongside the exact imperial era year.
- **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern X-Ray Lens**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents, or toggle the **X-Ray Lens** to project modern provincial boundaries directly over the historical map.
- **Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works**: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (*Yunmeng Marsh*, *Lop Nur / Puchanghai*), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era.

> [Try It Live: Ming Dynasty Yongle 13 (1415 CE) · Two Capitals, Thirteen Provinces & "Yingtian Prefecture" Inspection →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&zoom=1.75&center=115.8,33.2&hover=Yingtian%20Prefecture&lang=en)

![Ming Dynasty 1415 CE · Yingtian Prefecture Hover Preview](assets/preview_1415_ming_yingtian_en.webp)

---

### Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History (`Trace Place`)

**Click any ancient city or mountain pass** on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its **Trace Place** genealogy card:
- **Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy**: At the top of the card, read a curated **poetic epigraph and historical biography** for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with `Imperial Capital` badges and dynastic seat remarks.
- **Site-Specific Landmark Events**: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., *Shang Yang's Reforms* and *Qin's Unification* at Xianyang, *Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies* at Fancheng, the *Xuanwu Gate Incident* at Chang'an, or *Yue Fei's Martyrdom* at Lin'an). Click the **`Key Events`** pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year!
- **Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks**: Explore famous mountain passes—including *Hangu Pass*, *Tongguan*, *Jianmen Pass*, *Yanmen Pass*, *Yumen Pass*, *Yangguan*, and *Shanhai Pass*—rendered with traditional *Hanque* gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as *Red Cliffs (Chibi)*, *Gaixia*, *Wuzhang Plains*, *Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)*, *Yueyang Tower*, *Pavilion of Prince Teng*, *Languan Pass*, *Loulan*, *Lop Nur*, and *Issyk-Kul*.

> [Try It Live: High Tang Kaiyuan 29 (741 CE) · Open Chang'an's 2,400-Year Genealogy Card →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=Chang'an&lang=en)

![High Tang 741 CE · Chang'an Trace Place & Key Events](assets/preview_741_tang_trace_en.webp)

---

### Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space

Click the top-left **Universal Search Box** (with a rotatable `e.g.` figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as `Cao Cao`, `Huo Qubing`, `Sima Qian`, `Yue Fei`, or `Zheng He`) to open **Person Chronicle (`点人溯事`)**, plotting every milestone of their life with delicate cartographic hairline arcs and directional ticks across changing dynastic borders:
- **Qin Shi Huang's Unification Campaigns (238–221 BCE)**: From suppressing the rebellion at Xianyang and Wang Jian's attack on Ye, to the fall of Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu, and Dai, culminating in the surrender of Qi at Linzi—as you advance stop by stop, watch the six rival kingdoms merge into the Qin Empire right on the map!
- **Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE)**: Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi.
- **Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE)**: From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's *Memorial on Deploying the Troops*, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains.
- **Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE)**: Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an.
- **Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE)**: From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu.
- **Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE)**: From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the *Red Cliffs Rhapsody* in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island.
- **Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE)**: From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words *"This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?"* at Nan'an.

Each time you step to the next event (`‹ / ›`, `← / →`, or `Space` to auto-play), **the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps**, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site.

> [Try It Live: Follow Su Dongpo's Exile to Mizhou & Huangzhou (1075–1082 CE) →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en)

![Person Chronicle · Su Shi's Life & Exile Route](assets/preview_journey_sushi_en.webp)

---

### Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn?

Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click **`Quiz ›`** in the corner of the **Universal Search Box** guide bar (or type `quiz` for **`Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz`**):
- **Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing**: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by **dynastic historical clues** (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the on-pin **`✓ Confirm`** button to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates!
- Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as **Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家)**, **Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中)**, or **Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事)**.

> [Try It Live: Western Han Emperor Wu, Yuanshou 2 (121 BCE) · Start the Map Pinpoint Challenge →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en)

![Western Han 121 BCE · Map Pinpoint Challenge Preview](assets/preview_quiz_challenge_en.webp)

---

## Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links

### Keyboard Shortcuts

| Key / Action | Effect |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`/`** or **`Cmd/Ctrl + K`** | Focus the **Universal Search Box**: search **historical figures** (`Qin Shi Huang`/`Zhang Qian`/`Su Shi`), **ancient & modern cities** (`Xianyang`/`Chang'an`/`Luoyang`/`Kaifeng`), **reigning monarchs** (`Emperor Wu of Han`/`Taizong of Tang`/`Liu Che`/`Li Shimin`), **imperial eras** (`Zhenguan`/`Yongle`/`Kangxi`), **poetic & battlefield landmarks** (`Red Cliffs`/`Wuzhang Plains`/`Languan`/`Lanting`), **mountain passes** (`Hangu Pass`/`Jianmen Pass`/`Yumen Pass`), **historical events**, or the **Ancient Place Quiz** |

| **`Space`** | Auto-play / pause timeline evolution (or auto-advance stops in Person Chronicle mode) |
| **`Esc`** | Close active popups/cards, clear search highlights, or exit custom multi-stop routes |
| **`Single-click city` / `Double-click map`** | Open the 18-era **Trace Place & Key Events** genealogy card for that location |
| **`Hover / Click legend swatch`** | Hover to isolate & highlight that polity's territory; click to auto-zoom to its bounding box |

### Shareable Deep Links

Append query parameters to share any historical moment, battle, city genealogy, or multi-stop route:
- **Jump to a specific year or territorial shift**: [`?year=-403&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-403&lang=en) (403 BCE · Partition of Jin) / [`?year=-121&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&lang=en) (121 BCE · Huo Qubing opens the Hexi Corridor) / [`?year=648&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=648&lang=en) (648 CE · Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance in India) / [`?year=1288&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1288&lang=en) (1288 CE · Yuan Xuanzhengyuan over Tibet) / [`?year=1881&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1881&lang=en) (1881 CE · Zeng Jize recovers Ili) / [`?year=1945&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1945&lang=en) (1945 CE · Retrocession of Taiwan)
- **Pinpoint a famous battle**: [`?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en) (Battle of Changping) / [`?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en) (Battle of Red Cliffs) / [`?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en) (Battle of Fei River)
- **Inspect a city's 2,400-year genealogy**: [`?year=741&place=长安&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=长安&lang=en) (Chang'an / Xi'an) / [`?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en) (Jiankang / Yingtian / Nanjing) / [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en) (Han Yu at Languan Pass)

- **Open a person's spatio-temporal chronicle**: [`?person=qinshihuang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=qinshihuang&lang=en) (Qin Shi Huang) / [`?person=zhangqian&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhangqian&lang=en) (Zhang Qian) / [`?person=zhugeliang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhugeliang&lang=en) (Zhuge Liang) / [`?person=xuanzang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=xuanzang&lang=en) (Xuanzang) / [`?person=libai&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=libai&lang=en) (Li Bai) / [`?person=sushi&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) (Su Shi) / [`?person=wangyangming&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=wangyangming&lang=en) (Wang Yangming)
- **Start a quiz round**: [`?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) (Map Pinpoint Challenge)
- **Switch UI language**: [`?lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) (English) / [`?lang=zh-tw`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=zh-tw) (Traditional Chinese) / [`/`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/) (Simplified Chinese)

### Embed in Your Page

Put any view of the atlas into a blog post, Notion page, or course site:

1. Open the atlas and set up the view you want (a year, a regime profile, a place card, or a person's trajectory). The address bar always mirrors what you see.
2. Copy the URL and add `&embed=1`.
3. Paste it into an `<iframe>`:

```html
<iframe
  src="https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?embed=1&year=1104&trace=101.778,36.617&from=1072&to=1126&lang=en"
  width="100%" height="480" loading="lazy" style="border:0"
  title="Chronicles of the Realm · 1104 CE, Northern Song"></iframe>
```

The embedded map hides the site chrome and keeps only the map, a compact timeline, a title chip, an "Open in Jiangshan Atlas ↗" link, and a note that historical borders are approximate. Readers click once to start panning and zooming, so scrolling your page never gets stuck on the map.

| Parameter | Effect |
|---|---|
| `embed=1` | Turn on embed mode (required) |
| `year`, `polity`, `person`, `stop`, `trace`, `lang` | Same as the share links above |
| `from=1072&to=1126` | Limit the timeline to this range; the timeline zooms to show only it |
| `lock=1` | Freeze the map at `year` and hide the timeline |
| `autoplay=1` | Play a person's trajectory stop by stop (with `person`), or play the timeline |

WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, and Xiaohongshu do not allow iframes; share the plain link there instead.

---

## AI Agent, MCP & LLM Integration

**Chronicles of the Realm** works out of the box as a **historical-geography visualization engine for LLMs, MCP Clients, and AI Agents**. Models **never need to guess latitude/longitude coordinates**—simply extract two semantic parameters from a poem or historical text, **`year`** and **`place`**, and the atlas automatically resolves ancient/modern place names, centers the camera, renders dynastic borders and multi-stop trajectories, and opens the **Trace Place** genealogy card:

- **Machine-Readable Specification**: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt)
- **Zero-Dependency Local MCP Server (`stdio`)**: [`scripts/mcp_server.js`](scripts/mcp_server.js) — add to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Gemini CLI `mcpServers`:
  ```json

    "mcpServers": {
      "jiangshan-atlas": {
        "command": "node",
        "args": ["/absolute/path/to/jiangshan-map/scripts/mcp_server.js"]
      }
    }
  }
  ```
  Exposes 3 native MCP tools (`<5ms` offline response, zero npm dependencies):
  - `inspect_place({ year, place, lang? })`: Returns reigning monarch/era, controlling regime (`polity`), macro-region (`dao/lu/province`), prefecture (`jun/zhou/fu`), modern province/city, 2,400-year `lore`, and shareable deep-link URL.
  - `inspect_person({ person, stop?, lang? })`: Returns a historical figure or monarch's biography, chronological geocoded stops across dynasties, and shareable deep-link URL.
  - `search_atlas({ query, limit?, lang? })`: Searches across all ancient cities, poetic & battlefield landmarks, mountain passes, historical figures, imperial eras, and chronological milestones.

<p align="center">
  Open-source AI browser agent for chatting with pages, automating tasks, and running multi-step workflows with your choice of LLM.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/webbrain/ljhijonmfahplgbbacgcfnaihbjljhhb"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome-Install-4285F4?style=for-the-badge&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white" alt="Install WebBrain from the Chrome Web Store"></a>

![WebBrain reading a page, filling in a form, and fetching a file](assets/webbrain-demo.gif)

WebBrain is a web browser extension that puts an AI agent in a side panel next to
your tabs. Ask it about the page you're on, or hand it a task and let it click,
type, and navigate its way through. It runs on the model you choose — a local
llama.cpp or Ollama server, a frontier cloud API, or the managed default that
needs no setup at all.

## Install

Install from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/webbrain/ljhijonmfahplgbbacgcfnaihbjljhhb),
[Firefox Add-ons](https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/webbrain/), or
[Edge Add-ons](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/dfbioajafcijomhljabppcelecgdgfeo).

<details>
<summary><b>Or load it from source</b></summary>

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/webbrain-one/webbrain.git
```

**Chrome** — open `chrome://extensions/`, enable **Developer mode** (top
right), click **Load unpacked**, and select the `webbrain/src/chrome` folder.
For an isolated copy that won't pick up stray working-tree files, run
`npm run build:chrome` first and load `webbrain/build/chrome` instead.

**Firefox** — open `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox`, click **Load
Temporary Add-on**, and select `src/firefox/manifest.json` (or
`build/firefox/manifest.json` after `npm run build:firefox`). Temporary add-ons
are removed when Firefox restarts; permanent installation requires signing via
[addons.mozilla.org](https://addons.mozilla.org).

</details>

## Use it

Click the WebBrain icon to open the side panel, then type something like:

- "Summarize this page"
- "Find all links about pricing"
- "Fill in the search box with 'AI agents' and click Search"
- "Navigate to github.com and find trending repositories"

Three modes control what the agent is allowed to do:

| Mode    | What it can do                                                         |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Ask** | Read-only. Reads the page, answers questions, fetches URLs.            |
| **Act** | Clicks, types, navigates, uploads, downloads, fills forms.             |
| **Dev** | Adds page source, styles, console, network, and reversible page edits. |

WebBrain picks the mode for each message: it stays in Ask unless your message
asks it to do something in the browser. Start a message with `/ask`, `/act` or
`/dev` to choose the mode yourself.

## Pick a model

**WebBrain Compass 1.0** is the default and needs no API key or local setup.

**Local models** need no API key either. Point WebBrain at any OpenAI-compatible
server:

```bash
llama-server -m your-model.gguf --port 8080          # llama.cpp
ollama serve                                          # Ollama  → :11434/v1
vllm serve your-model --port 8000                     # vLLM    → :8000/v1
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path your-model --port 30000
```

LM Studio (`:1234/v1`), Osaurus (`:1337/v1`), Jan (`:1337/v1`), LocalAI (`:8080/v1`), and GPT4All
(`:4891/v1`) work the same way. **WebBrain Companion** is our separate desktop
app for local models and supported account subscriptions. [Download it for
Windows, macOS, or Linux](https://github.com/webbrain-one/webbrain/releases/tag/systray-v0.1.2),
then choose the **WebBrain Companion** provider card, click **Load Models**,
select a model, and test the connection. The local endpoint defaults to
`http://127.0.0.1:8327/v1` and needs no API key on this computer. See the
[Companion setup](docs/providers-and-models.md#webbrain-companion).
A generic **Local OpenAI-compatible Proxy** card remains available for other
OpenAI-compatible gateways.
**Unsloth Studio (Local)** uses the same OpenAI-compatible path with the Studio
port and `sk-unsloth-` API key configured by the user; see the
[Unsloth Studio setup](docs/providers-and-models.md#unsloth-studio).
**Osaurus (Local)** connects to the Mac's Osaurus server with model discovery,
streaming, and tool calls; see the [Osaurus setup](docs/providers-and-models.md#osaurus).
Size the loaded context window for the selected tier's system prompt and tool
schemas, the page/history, and the requested output. **16k is a configuration
fallback, not a guaranteed minimum; Compact is not guaranteed to fit 8k.**
Mid and Full can exceed 16k before history accumulates, and compaction cannot
shrink fixed instructions or schemas. The sizing estimate is not the model's
exact tokenizer; see the [context guidance](docs/providers-and-models.md#local-providers).
WebBrain auto-detects the real window for llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM
Studio, and auto-compacts the conversation as it fills up. For Ollama,
llama.cpp, LM Studio, and LocalAI, it also reads native server metadata before
adding screenshots; the Providers page provides Auto, Force on, and Off overrides. When
the optional Model field is blank, the loaded-model capability is rechecked on
every user turn so a server-side hot swap takes effect. There is also a
preview `ollama launch webbrain --model <model>` handoff. Details:
[providers and models](docs/providers-and-models.md#local-providers).

**Cloud APIs** — OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS
Bedrock, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI Grok, MiniMax, Kimi, Qwen, z.ai GLM, Groq,
Together, Cloudflare, Nvidia NIM, Hugging Face, Fireworks, OpenRouter, and more.
The Providers page ships **119 built-in provider cards on Chromium** (118 on Firefox),
including an endpoint-free local WebGPU option with the tested LFM2.5 2.6B
preset and an experimental custom Hugging Face ONNX repository option —
see the [full catalog](docs/providers-and-models.md#extended-provider-catalog).

For a local or bring-your-own provider, the per-provider **Share queries for
research** switch remains off by default. When enabled, it now shares a
bounded, content-free diagnostic timeline for that provider's model attempts
(including failed runs) alongside the existing scrubbed prompt/response share.
The timeline includes tool names, outcomes, error codes, and timings, but not
tool arguments, page content, or screenshots. If a run fails before a normal
generation share, its bounded model-facing request and final blocker accompany
the diagnostic record. No second sharing switch is
required; turning the existing switch off also purges queued diagnostics.

## Features

- **Reads any page** — text, links, forms, tables, PDFs, and interactive
  elements, via the accessibility tree rather than brittle selectors
- **Acts on it** — click, type, scroll, navigate, upload, download, and verify
  forms, with per-site permission prompts before consequential actions
- **Vision mode** (aka "Tesla" mode) — vision only, like a Tesla on cameras: with a model that
  takes images, Act runs see the page as screenshots and click, type and scroll at coordinates; only the changed part
  of the screen is sent after each action, and retina displays and browser
  zoom are handled ([details](docs/vision-mode.md))
- **Plan before Act** — Act and Dev can generate a structured plan, show it for
  approval, and pin the approved plan to the scratchpad before any tool runs
- **Multi-step agent** — autonomous tool-use loop, configurable up to 195 steps
  (default 130), with a Continue button when it hits the limit
- **Saved workflows** — turn a successful run into a reusable, value-free
  workflow you can re-run, export, and share
- **Scheduled tasks and watches** — `/schedule` for later, `/watch` to poll a
  page and act when a condition is met
- **Skills** — trusted instructions and tools that load only when relevant
- **Smart context** — token-aware auto-compaction, tool-result limits, and
  emergency overflow recovery
- **Per-tab conversations** — each tab keeps its own history; optional local
  user memory for stated preferences
- **Optional cross-device recall** — connect MemCode with OAuth for read-only
  lookup while local memory stays the default ([setup and privacy](docs/memcode-recall.md))
- **Reading-first side panel** — streaming Ask replies, floating controls that
  keep your question in view as answers grow, copy buttons, a page-inspection
  banner, and a stop button that works mid-run
- **Deterministic by default** — temperature `0.15` for browser-control
  decisions, `0.3` for Ask, `0` for vision screenshot descriptions

## Agent tools

WebBrain separates **tier** from **mode**. Tier (`compact`, `mid`, `full`) is a
per-provider setting controlling how many tools a model sees — Compact suits
small local models, Full unlocks hover, drag-drop, frames, and shadow DOM. Mode
(`ask`, `act`, `dev`) controls what the user is allowing.

The full tool-by-tier matrix, WebMCP notes, and Dev-mode diagnostics are in
[agent tools](docs/agent-tools.md).

## Slash commands

Type `/help` in the panel for full signatures and flags. The most useful ones:

| Command                                                                                | What it does                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/ask` · `/act` · `/dev` · `/plan`                                                     | Switch mode before sending                                                  |
| `/schedule [prompt]`                                                                   | Create a scheduled task                                                     |
| `/watch [--keep] [--secs <30-120>] [--long \| --short] <condition and action> [/beep]` | Poll the current page and act when a condition is met                       |
| `/workflow` · `/workflow --save <name>`                                                | Manage saved workflows or compile the last successful run                   |
| `/teach --start <name>` · `/teach --end`                                               | Learn a reusable workflow from your demonstrated actions                    |
| `/memory --add <text>`                                                                 | Save a user preference                                                      |
| `/screenshot [--full-page]`                                                            | Capture the tab, or the full scrollable page                                |
| `/record [--transcribe]`                                                               | Record the current tab, optionally saving a transcript                      |
| `/export [--traces \| --config]`                                                       | Download the conversation, tool chain, or a Settings snapshot               |
| `/compact` · `/reset` · `/verbose`                                                     | Compact context, clear the conversation, toggle tool detail                 |
| `/allow-api`                                                                           | Per-conversation override letting `fetch_url` mutate when the UI is failing |

`/watch` runs its first check immediately, then polls every 60 seconds
(`--secs` accepts 30–120). Relative conditions like "when a new commit appears"
establish a baseline on the first check; `--keep` keeps the watch running and
suppresses repeated alerts for the same stable event key.

Full reference, including `/dangerously-skip-permissions` and the run-capture
suffixes: [slash commands](docs/slash-commands.md).

## Keyboard Shortcuts

Chrome side panel shortcuts work when the WebBrain side panel has focus.

| Shortcut                        | What it does                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Ctrl+/` or `Cmd+/`             | Focus the input                                                              |
| `Ctrl+Shift+A` or `Cmd+Shift+A` | Start the message with `/ask`                                                |
| `Ctrl+Shift+X` or `Cmd+Shift+X` | Start the message with `/act`                                                |
| `Ctrl+Shift+D` or `Cmd+Shift+D` | Start the message with `/dev`                                                |
| `Escape`                        | Stop the active run, unless it is only dismissing slash-command autocomplete |
| `Escape` twice                  | Stop an active recording from WebBrain or browser pages                      |

Also available in [中文](docs/zh-CN/) and [Français](docs/fr/).

## Community

Chat about everything WebBrain — help, local and cloud model setups, site
adapters, show-and-tell, and contributor coordination — on the
[WebBrain Discord](https://discord.gg/cgC325ssfw). See
[community](docs/community.md) for how the server is organized, and
[discord-setup](docs/discord-setup.md) for the channel, role, and welcome-screen
configuration. Bug reports and feature requests belong in
[GitHub issues](https://github.com/webbrain-one/webbrain/issues), not Discord.

## Repository layout

```
src/chrome/     Manifest V3 build — service worker, chrome.scripting, sidePanel
src/firefox/    Manifest V2 build — background page, executeScript, sidebar_action
docs/           Design and reference docs (en, zh-CN, fr)
mcp-server/     MCP server — delegate browser tasks from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor
lmstudio-plugin/  Web tools + browser delegation as a standalone LM Studio plugin
web/            Landing site and docs site
test/           Node test suite, LLM scenario benchmarks, security corpora
```

Nearly all agent code is shared between the two builds. See
[architecture](docs/architecture.md#chrome-vs-firefox-key-differences) for where
they diverge.

## Known issues

**Firefox is meaningfully weaker than Chrome.** Firefox has no equivalent to the
Chrome DevTools Protocol via `chrome.debugger`, so the Firefox build has no
shadow-DOM piercing, no real trusted mouse events (some React/Vue handlers won't
fire), no closed-shadow-root traversal, no `resolveSelector` retry budget, no
SPA-navigation-aware retry, and no CDP screenshots. It uses `tabs.captureTab`
for viewport screenshots, including inactive run tabs, but still cannot provide
Chrome's pixel-perfect or full-page CDP capture. Site adapters, vision
detection, loop detection, the auto-screenshot loop, and the Compact prompt/tool
set _are_ mirrored to Firefox. Some single-page apps may also fail to trigger
content-script re-injection after client-side navigation.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). To add a tool, follow the checklist in
[adding a tool](docs/adding-a-tool.md). To add a provider, subclass
`BaseLLMProvider`, implement `chat()` (and optionally `chatStream()`), and
register it in `providers/manager.js` — mirroring both changes to
`src/chrome/` and `src/firefox/`. All providers normalize to
`{ content, toolCalls, usage }`; details in
[providers and models](docs/providers-and-models.md#adding-a-provider).

Recent changes are in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## MCP server

Let a coding agent use *your* browser. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenClaw
can delegate a task to WebBrain running in the session you are already signed
into — cookies present, SSO already passed. A headless framework starts logged
out and stalls at the first login wall; this does not.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio webbrain -- npx -y @webbrain/mcp-server
```

## Install a Plugin

For most users, the **Awesome Copilot** marketplace is already registered in the Copilot CLI/VS Code, so you can install a plugin directly:

```bash
copilot plugin install <plugin-name>@awesome-copilot
```

If you are using an older Copilot CLI version or a custom setup and see an error that the marketplace is unknown, register it once and then install:

```bash
copilot plugin marketplace add github/awesome-copilot
copilot plugin install <plugin-name>@awesome-copilot
```

README

# dsh-memory-evolve 使用场景指南

> **一句话**：让 DSH 里的 AI 拥有跨会话的长期记忆、帮你管理待办与技能、还能拉起一群 AI 会话和外部 AI 代理协同干活——**越用越懂你，换会话不丢上下文**。
>
> 本指南按真实工作流组织，每个场景讲「适合谁、能做什么、怎么用、会得到什么」。
>
> 相关文档：[详细功能说明](README-详细说明.md) · [记忆同步](docs/记忆同步.md) · [更新日志](docs/CHANGELOG.md) · [English](README.en.md)

---

## 快速开始（安装）

插件包内自带 `cordis.patch.yml`（`dsh.bundle.patch` 声明），`dsh plugin add` 安装后 **host 端自动注册，无需任何手动配置**。以 web profile 为例，两步装好：

```sh
# 1. 安装到 profile（本地目录用 link:，也可用 git/registry 包地址）
dsh plugin --profile web add github:csyangwen/dsh-memory-evolve

# 2. 重启 dsh web 即生效
```

> ⚠️ **不要再往 `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` 手动 insert 本插件**：bundle patch 已自动注册，重复 insert 同 id 会让加载器报 duplicate loader entry id 无法启动。完整说明见 [详细功能说明](README-详细说明.md)「标准安装」章节。

**修改默认配置**（如开启回合内记忆审查）：在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 用 id 覆盖（顶层写法，非 insert）：

```yaml
- id: dsh-memory-evolve
  config:
    reviewEnabled: true      # 开启回合内记忆审查（默认关）
    reviewInterval: 10       # 每 10 个用户回合审查一次
```

**插件异常导致 DSH 无法启动时，临时禁用**（等修复后取消）：同样在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 加一行即可，无需卸载：

```yaml
- id: dsh-memory-evolve
  disabled: true
```

**从旧版本升级**：若你此前按旧文档手动 insert 过本插件，请删除 profile patch 里的 insert 行（否则与 bundle 自动注册重复）。

卸载：`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-memory-evolve`，一切效果随插件卸载自动清理。

---

## 认识它（30 秒）

装上插件后，打开任意会话，你会多出一排能力标签：**记忆 · 技能 · 待办 · 无限画板 · COI 调度 · 会话广播 · 提示词 · 记忆同步 · 模型设置 · 书签 · 会话评审 · Web UI 设置 · Memory Evolve 设置**。AI 侧则多了一批工具：记忆读写、待办、技能管理、本地文件搜索、会话编排、会话广播、外部 AI 派单、提示词注入、模型查询……

一句话概括这些能力：**让 AI 记住你、替你管、替你做、互相配合做。**

> 小提示：插件里很多能力默认关闭（不占 AI 的工具清单），需要时在「Memory Evolve 设置」里打开即可。下面的场景大多是组合玩法——**把相关功能都打开，才能串成完整的流水线**。

---

## 场景一：让 AI 真正记住你（长期记忆）

**适合谁**：所有人。这是插件的核心，也是其他一切功能的地基。

AI 的对话是「一次性」的：换项目、隔几天、开新会话，它就忘了你是谁。插件的五轨记忆让 AI 拥有**跨会话的长期工作记忆**：

- **用户档案**：你的偏好、公司、沟通习惯——AI 每回合都能看到；
- **全局事实**：环境、工具、惯例等长期知识；
- **项目关键记忆**：当前项目的约定、决策、架构、踩坑，自动注入上下文，重要结论可标记**只在某个 git 分支生效**；
- **项目日志 / 每日日志**：每回合自动记录进展，按需读取，历史可追溯。

**怎么用**：

1. 正常和 AI 对话即可——每回合结束时它会自动把进展写进项目日志和今日日志；
2. 发现重要事实时对它说「**记一下：这个项目的部署端口是 8080**」，它会写入项目关键记忆，**你确认后**才生效——AI 不会擅自往记忆里写东西；
3. 过几天、换了个会话，直接问「**查一下记忆，上次我们定下的架构决策是什么**」——它能无缝衔接；
4. 记忆多了之后，让 AI「**把 XX 那条记忆归档**」——归档条目不再注入上下文，随时可转回；
5. **情绪反馈记录**：你对工作结果的评价（如「太好了」「怎么还没改对」）会被 AI 记入当日与项目日志（`【反馈】` 行，含情绪、任务分类、你的原话）——积累后随时可以让 AI「**分析一下最近我对哪些方面不满意**」，判断它在哪类任务上做得好/不好。

**会得到什么**：AI 从一个「每次会话都失忆」的对话机器，变成了解你全盘工作的长期伙伴——隔天继续开发，它直接引用昨天的结论，不用你复述。

---

## 场景：多台电脑共享项目记忆（记忆同步）

**适合谁**：办公室和家里两台电脑干活、或有同事协作同一个项目的人——不想在每台电脑上把重要结论重新讲一遍。

**怎么用**（详见 [记忆同步](docs/记忆同步.md)）：

1. 「Memory Evolve 设置 → 配置」打开「**记忆同步**」模块开关（这只是让功能可见）；
2. 在项目会话的「**记忆同步**」Tab 打开「**本项目同步**」——点「开始同步」即可（记忆远端默认用你的代码仓库，自动存进专属分支，不污染代码），再点「同步并推送」完成首次推送；**代码公开（如 GitHub 开源）但记忆想私藏**？填一个**共享记忆仓库**地址——一个仓库装所有项目的记忆（每项目一条专属分支），记忆与代码彻底隔离；
3. 另一台电脑 clone 项目后打开——**自动认亲**（同一仓库地址 = 同一项目），拉下来即可继续用；
4. 平时照常写记忆（实时落盘、零延迟），攒一批点一次「同步」；两台电脑都改了同一条记忆才会出现冲突，Tab 里选「采用本机 / 采用远端 / 两者都要」即可。

**会得到什么**：项目关键记忆、项目日志、归档、项目待办跨设备一致；填了共享记忆仓库后，**全局记忆（用户档案/每日日志/待办）也能跨设备**（四个独立轨开关，开哪个同步哪个）——换电脑不换记忆。**没开同步的项目完全不受影响**（保持纯本地状态）。

---

## 场景二：多项目并行开发，每件事都不丢（待办 + 项目日志 + 本地搜索）

**适合谁**：同时维护多个项目、经常被「之前那个方案是怎么定的」卡住的开发者。

- **四轨待办**：生活 / 工作 / 项目 / 每日。「项目」轨按工作目录隔离，换目录互不干扰。说「**记住，周五前把二级面板部署到手机访问实例**」，自动落成项目待办（带重要/紧急、截止日期）；每天收尾 AI 会提醒你到期的待办；
- **项目日志**：每个项目的进展按目录隔离沉淀，日志自动带 `[git main]` 分支标记，可溯源；
- **本地文件搜索**：对 AI 说「**搜一下本机有没有写过类似的东西**」——按文件名找文档（可扩展到全类型）；也能内容检索：「**哪个文档里提过 XX**」直接返回命中文件和片段。

**怎么用**：

1. 新项目开工直接开聊，项目日志自动建档；
2. 冒出的想法对 AI 说「记住」，它会进待确认队列——到「待办」里**采纳或拒绝**，你说了算；
3. 想不起来就问「之前有个文档提到过 XX」。

**会得到什么**：同时开 3 个项目也不乱——每个项目的记忆、待办、文档线索各归各的目录，问一句就能捡起来。

---

## 场景三：一个人指挥一群 AI 干活（内部团队）

**适合谁**：想把 AI 用成「团队」的人——一个主会话指挥美工、前端、后端、测试多个子会话。

**怎么用**：

1. **拉起团队**：对主会话的 AI 说「**创建 4 个会话：美工负责网站视觉、前端负责页面、后端负责接口、测试负责验收，把它们拉进同一个协作房间**」——它立刻创建 4 个标准会话（出现在左侧列表、随时可接管），自动继承你的模型与工作目录；创建时可指定 **Agent 预设**（如「用代码模式创建前端会话」），决定该会话的工具面与人格；
2. **协作沟通**：房间建好后，**谁改了什么、谁干完了，全员可见**；成员状态（正在生成 / 空闲）变化会自动收到「房间动态」通知；**房间消息可以带图片**——截图直接发群里，接收方 AI 通过 read 拿到图片文件路径，可读图、可转发到 IM 渠道；
3. **派活与催活**：问 AI「**现在谁在干活、谁空闲了**」，它会查看各会话状态；对空闲的会话说「**叫前端把结果发过来**」，AI 自动唤醒它并派活——不会批量自动唤醒，一切由你（或你的主会话）有意识地指挥；
4. **防冲突**：同一项目多个会话并行改代码时，开工前对 AI 说「**声明一下你要改哪些文件**」——其他人（及其 AI）能看到「谁在改什么」；真撞车了，写入方会收到冲突警告，还有「工作区活动」通知（并行开始/结束、成员变化时单独推送）随时告知谁在跑、在干什么；
5. **结果回传**：各成员干完把结果发回房间，你汇总确认。

**持续运转（关键）**：主会话自己一直在运行，所以它能**随时唤醒已经休息（空闲）的会话继续干活**——催活、收结果、派下一轮，哪怕你不在电脑前，队伍也能一路推进到出结果。唯一的前提是**主会话所在的 DSH 进程保持运行**；如果主会话空闲了或 DSH 被关掉，唤醒链就停了——需要你回来发一条消息，队伍重新开动。

**会得到什么**：一个人的开发产出，变成一个小团队的吞吐。任务交接、唤醒、冲突预警全链路自动化，房间消息留痕可查。

---

## 场景四：重活派给外部 AI 代理（外部外援）

**适合谁**：需要把大任务（视觉重设计、代码审查、完整功能开发）交给专用 AI 代理（Kimi / Codex / Grok / Hermes）的用户——不想被阻塞，又不想错过结果。

**怎么用**：

1. 对 AI 说「**把这个任务派给 grok：移动端适配改造**」——后台异步执行，立即返回任务号，**不卡当前会话**，你可以继续聊别的；
2. 期间随时问「**任务进度如何**」，或在「COI 调度」里看实时日志流；
3. 派单时 AI 可自主选择带上你的项目记忆——外部代理也「懂项目约定」；
4. **派单可以带图**：对 AI 说「**把这张截图发给 grok 分析**」——附件支持本地路径/远程 URL/本会话图片（你在输入框贴的图），codex/kimi/hermes 都能真看图（grok 走 prompt 读图，zcode 纯文本会明确拒绝）；
5. 完成后结果摘要**自动写入项目日志与今日日志**——派出去的活自动变成你的记忆资产。

**会得到什么**：AI 派活给 AI，你只负责确认验收。视觉改版、深度代码审查、批量重构这类「重活」都能甩出去，主会话保持轻快。

---

## 场景五：内外协同——一支队伍，两种兵种

**适合谁**：任务大到单靠一边搞不定的人。这是插件协作能力的完全体：**内部会话负责「需要上下文和来回打磨的活」，外部代理负责「一次性重活」，两者通过记忆、房间、提示词串成一条流水线。**

一个完整的真实流程（产品视觉改版）：

1. **分工**：主会话 spawn 前端、测试两个内部会话并拉进房间；同时把「全站视觉重设计」派给外部代理 Kimi；
2. **外部主刀**：Kimi 后台跑重设计（不占任何会话）；期间内部前端会话先做数据层和页面结构，不干等；
3. **接力**：Kimi 完成，摘要自动沉淀进项目记忆——主会话把设计结论发到房间，前端会话**读记忆拿到设计规范**，开始集成；
4. **问题升级**：集成中发现一个诡异样式问题，前端会话卡住——主会话把这个 bug 派给 Grok 深挖，结论回房间，前端会话照结论修复；
5. **验收**：测试会话跑完验收流程，结果发回房间，你最后确认。

协作的四个结合点，可以自由组合：

- **任务接力**：外部代理的产出（摘要/结论）自动进记忆 → 内部会话接力执行——**外部做重活，内部做集成与打磨**；
- **问题升级**：内部会话遇到难啃的问题 → 主会话派给外部代理深挖 → 结论回房间——**内部快节奏迭代，外部慢工出细活**；
- **标准统一**：给外部代理派活时，注入你沉淀的提示词（如「代码审查清单」「PRD 规范」）——**外部代理按你的流程干活，不靠运气**；
- **状态同步**：谁在跑、谁干完了，房间 + 工作区活动 + 通知随时可见——**你不用当人肉调度员**。

**会得到什么**：一条「外部主刀 → 内部集成 → 测试验收 → 你确认」的完整流水线。大任务不再是一个人（或一个 AI）硬扛，而是内外两支队伍分工协作。

## 场景六：AI 的自我纪律——提示词注入

**适合谁**：想把「好用的工作方法」沉淀下来、让每个 AI（包括外部代理）都按同一套流程干活的人。

提示词库是**指令范式资产库**：代码审查、调试、PRD、测试策略……把常用的工作方法固化成提示词（可分类、可搜索、可启用/禁用）。

**怎么用**：

1. **AI 自己选、自己注入**：AI 觉得当前任务适用某套流程时，它会自己查看提示词库、选中合适的提示词注入自己——「接下来按代码审查清单执行」；下一轮它自动遵循，**不打断当前回复**；也能「立即注入」，当前回合马上生效；
2. **你一键注入**：在「提示词注入」里选中一条，点「注入一次 / 持续注入 / 立即注入」——持续注入就是「每回合提醒 AI 按此纪律干活」；
3. **临时注入**：不建提示词，直接输入一段要求注入，自动存入库中，下次复用；
4. **派活带纪律**：给子会话、外部代理派活时，让 AI 把对应提示词一起带上——**整个团队用同一套标准**。

**会得到什么**：好方法不再只存在你脑子里或一次对话里——它变成可复用的「团队操作手册」，AI 会主动遵守，你只管维护手册质量。

## 场景七：会话太长、太贵、容易糊——书签与分支

**适合谁**：对上下文开销敏感、一个会话动辄上百轮的深度用户。

- **会话书签**：每一轮都可以点星（☆）标记，「书签」列出全部书签（名称/轮次/时间/摘要，可搜索），**点击一键跳回任意一轮**——探索到「这个结论很重要」就打个星；
- **任意轮分支**：官方只支持从最后一轮创建分支；本插件把**中间任意轮的分支入口接管**——书签列表点「分支」（或直接点官方分支按钮，中间轮会弹出确认），走官方分支通道创建新会话，进入官方分支谱系；
- **上下文占用提醒**：输入框圆环实时显示上下文占用——≥30% 变黄、≥40% 变红，提醒你该打书签、该开分支、该开新会话了。

**怎么用**：

1. 探索性会话在关键轮次点 ☆，给书签起个名字（如「方案 A 评审结论」）；
2. 想从中间某个决策点另开一条线，书签列表点「分支」；
3. 看到圆环变红，把当前会话打个书签，开新会话继续。

**会得到什么**：上下文不再是一根只能从头滚到尾的绳子，而是**带锚点、可分支、可跳转的时间线**——每一轮的探索成果都能被精准复用，不会再因为「会话太长了」被迫放弃中间的好结论。

## 场景八：离开电脑也能用（手机访问 + 会话筛选 + 通知）

**适合谁**：离开电脑也想继续和 AI 协作、或者同时开很多会话看不过来的人。

- **手机浏览器访问**：DSH 界面适配了手机——对话区/消息气泡满宽、输入栏「⋯」上拉收纳工具栏与模型选择，手机上操作和电脑端一致；
- **会话列表筛选**：左侧列表可只显示「进行中的会话」，一屏看清谁在干活——桌面端同样适用；
- **渠道通知（de_notify）**：对 AI 说「任务完成用飞书通知我」，重要结果推到飞书/QQ/微信/企业微信，电脑前/手机上立刻知道（通知内容带「这是通知」标注，可附图片/文件）；
- **web 站内通知（de_notify channels=web）**：对 AI 说「发个站内通知给我」，通知直接落到**网页右上角的铃铛**——未读数字徽标 + 弹窗列表，能看到「哪个会话发来什么」，点主题跳转到那个会话、长内容点「查看详情」打开大弹窗看全文；铃铛可随意拖动、松手吸附到屏幕左/右边缘（位置记忆）。发到 web 和发到飞书等 IM 是同一句话，只是换个送达目的地（channels 传 `web`，或 `all` 一起发）；
- **渠道直发（de_channel_send）**：AI 随时主动把文本/图片/文件发到你的 IM 渠道（不带通知标注）——「把生成的图片/文档发给我」类场景；四个渠道（飞书/QQ/微信/企微）全部支持，附件来源可选本地路径/远程 URL/内联 base64/**本会话图片**（sessionImage=true 直接转发你在 DSH 输入框粘贴/拖入发送的图；attachmentId 显式引用，配合 de_session_images 先查本会话有哪些图，需 DSH 260810+ 快照）。

**会得到什么**：重活照派、进度照盯，人不用守在电脑前——回电脑后从左侧列表接管会话继续。

## 场景九：给每个会话配一个隐形评审员（会话评审）

**适合谁**：想让 AI 干活时有一双"第二眼睛"把关、又不想自己逐句盯的人——尤其是项目里定了纪律（如"回复前先说明自己在哪个目录"）却总发现 AI 聊着聊着就忘了的情况。

**能做什么**：

- **独立评审员**：给每个会话挂一个独立的评审会话，它**只观察你在界面上看到的对话**（用户说的话 + Agent 的回复正文），看不到思考过程、工具调用参数等内部细节——像旁边坐了一位只旁听对话、不碰键盘的同事；
- **每轮实时评审**：对话每推进一轮，评审员就基于**完整上下文**评审一次——它是持续会话，像普通 LLM 长对话一样记住全部历史、**永不截断**，不会"忘了前面说过什么"；
- **需要时实时提醒（steer）**：评审员发现值得说的点，会以**用户指令的形式**注入当前会话——Agent 会把它当成你说的话直接执行（2026-08-13 拍板：实测带"非用户指令"标记会让 Agent 质疑来源、执行力下降，所以伪装成用户指令效果最好）；GUI 对话流中这类消息显示为**折叠行 `[severity]` 前缀**，方便你一眼认出哪些话其实是评审员说的；
- **四级严重度**：`info`（仅记录、默认不注入主会话，可配置注入）/ `nit`（小建议）/ `concern`（值得处理）/ `blocker`（必须立即处理）——不是所有话都打断，只有该说的才说；
- **新建评审会话**：面板里一键清空评审员的上下文与记忆重来——新会话第一条指令由你告诉它背景，上下文长度由你掌控；
- **直接向评审员提问**：面板里随时提问，它立即回答（回答只在评审面板展示，不注入主会话流）——像随时可以问的旁听同事；
- **四层级约束**：系统提示词（全局默认，可查看全文/修改/一键恢复）/ **项目约束**（本工作区共享）/ **会话约束**（本会话保留）/ **本次评审会话约束**（随"新建评审会话"清空）——四层拼接注入，冲突时越局部越优先；
- **记录可查**：评审记录 JSONL 持久化，面板「记录」可追溯。

**怎么用**：

1. 「Memory Evolve 设置 → 配置」打开「**会话评审**」（`advisorEnabled`，默认关闭）；评审模型缺省继承当前会话模型，也可单独配置 `advisorProvider`/`advisorModel`；
2. 会话页出现「会话评审」悬浮窗，点开面板即可看到评审员的实时评审流与上下文占用；
3. 在「约束」Tab 给评审员立规矩（如项目约束："每次回复前先说明自己在哪个目录"），保存立即生效；
4. 想让评审员重头开始就点「**新建评审会话**」；想直接问它就点「**提问**」；
5. Agent 侧：评审提醒以折叠行 `[severity]` 出现在对话流里——你能看到评审员说了什么、Agent 是否照做。

**会得到什么**：每个 AI 会话都多了一位持续在岗的"旁听同事"——它不打断你的节奏，只在关键时刻以你的口吻提醒 Agent 纠偏；项目纪律、会话约束有人替你盯着，不会聊着聊着就忘了规矩。

## 场景十：散落的素材，一块画板装下（无限画板）

**适合谁**：设计稿在下载目录、合同在文档库、参考图在桌面、录音在个人文件夹——每次要用都得开 Finder 一层层翻的人；以及想让 AI"看得见"你手头素材、又不想把素材一股脑塞进对话上下文的人。

**能做什么**：

- **素材集中上板**：三种入口——**路径上板**（粘贴本地路径）、**便签**（画板内直接写，内容不落盘）、**搜索上板**（真实搜本机文件，搜到一键上板）；文本类文件上板后自动读取内容；
- **一眼看见**：无限平移/缩放画布，卡片自由摆放、右下角拖拽调大小；图片/音视频/文本在画板内直接预览，Word/PDF 等走系统默认应用打开；
- **单板 + 视角筛选**：物理上一块画板，节点带归属徽标（🌐 全局 / 📁 项目 / 💬 会话）；默认会话视角看"自己会话 + 当前项目 + 全局"，切「项目」看该项目全部会话，切「全局」看所有；
- **快速调用**：复制节点 ID / 标题 / 路径 / 引用串（`[canvas:id] 标题`），把引用串丢给 AI，它就能凭 id 找到素材；
- **AI 双向（拉取式）**：AI 用 `de_canvas` 工具按 id 查画板、读素材内容、往画板中央区放便签（带「AI 放置」标记）——**画板内容不注入上下文**，需要时主动查，省 token 不打扰；
- **本地路径引用**：文件留在原地，画板只记"指向哪里"——源文件改动实时可见，删除源文件后卡片显示失效提示；
- **安全边界**：AI 只能读**已上板**的节点（没有任意路径读取 API）；敏感目录（.ssh/.config 等）即使上板也拒绝代理。

**怎么用**：

1. 「Memory Evolve 设置 → 配置」打开「**无限画板**」（`canvasEnabled`，默认关闭）；
2. 会话页出现「画板」Tab：路径上板 / 便签 / 搜索上板，卡片自由摆；
3. 点卡片「引用」复制引用串，对 AI 说"去画板拿 XX"——AI 用 `de_canvas` 查/读/放便签；
4. AI 放的便签落在画板中央虚线区，拖到想要的位置即可。

**会得到什么**：告别"文件在哪来着"的反复翻找——素材集中一块画板，人和 AI 在同一张桌子上干活：你摆、AI 拿；AI 放、你看。

## 发布版本

插件使用 **git tag** 作为发布版本标识（两种格式都支持：**日期戳 `v<纯数字>`** 如 `v26081302`（日常发版推荐）、语义化 `v1.2.3`）：日常开发推送 main 分支不会触发任何更新提示，只有打了发布 tag 才会被各设备检测到。

**发版流程（开发者）**：

```bash
# 1. 提交并推送 main（tag 必须打在已推送的 main 提交上）
git push origin main

# 2. 用发版脚本一键完成：工作树/远端同步检查 → 构建 → 全量测试 → 打 annotated tag → 推送 tag
bash ~/shell/dsh-memory-evolve-release.sh v26081302 -m "发布说明：……"
```

**各设备更新（使用者）**：

- 进入 Web UI 后自动检测（24 小时内最多自动检测一次，也可点「检查更新」强制检测；插件启动时也会后台检测一次）；
- 检测到新版本时，设置 Tab 出现 🔴 红点；进入「版本」页点击「更新到 v26081302」；
- 更新完成后**必须重启 dsh web 再刷新浏览器**（仅刷新页面不会加载新代码）；
- 更新后插件处于 detached HEAD（跟随发布 tag）：继续用「版本」页的更新按钮升级即可，**不要直接 `git pull`**；
- 想回到开发轨：`git checkout main && git pull --ff-only`。

**更新安全机制**：只接受严格格式（v<纯数字> 或 v1.2.3）且位于 origin/main 历史的 tag；更新前校验本地工作树干净；更新过程有跨进程锁与失败回滚，不会把半更新状态留给你。

## 三条原则

1. **AI 只提议，你确认**：AI 自建的记忆、待办、技能都先进待确认队列——所有会真实改变 AI 行为的写入，决定权都在你；
2. **不重复造轮子**：官方已有的能力不碰，只做官方没做、且真实解决痛点的；
3. **内外有别、协作互补**：内部会话负责需要上下文的活，外部代理负责一次性重活，记忆、房间、提示词把它们串成一条流水线。
